title: Indonesia's stock index falls about 11% after MSCI proposes a downgrade
dek: Reports call it the biggest one-day drop since 1998. MSCI wants to move Indonesia out of the emerging-market group.
what: The Jakarta Composite Index fell by roughly 11 percent on Friday, October 16. Business Today reports a drop of about 614 points to close near 5,240. Other search results gave a close of 5,185 and a fall of 11.57 percent. I could not reconcile the two, so the exact figure is not settled here.
Business Today reports the index is down about 39 percent for the year after the fall, and that it was the worst day since January 1998.

The cause reported is a proposal from MSCI, the index provider, to reclassify Indonesia from an emerging market to a standalone market. Business Today quotes MSCI citing "persistent opacity in shareholding structures and suspected coordinated trading behavior." It says a consultation is open and a final decision is due by the end of June 2027.

Business Today says the Indonesian authorities had announced reforms, including more disclosure by large shareholders and a roadmap toward a 15 percent minimum free float, but that MSCI has not seen sufficient progress consistently. I did not find a statement from Indonesian officials on Friday's fall.
why: A fall this size in a large market is rare. Funds that track MSCI indexes could have to sell if a downgrade goes ahead, which is how outlets describe the risk; I did not check that against MSCI's documents.
common: Established by the outlet cited: a fall of about 11 percent on October 16, and an MSCI proposal to reclassify Indonesia. Not settled: the exact close, and how much selling by funds would follow a downgrade.
next: MSCI's consultation is open, with a final decision by the end of June 2027, per Business Today.

sources.label: Business Today: Jakarta Composite plunges as MSCI reviews emerging market status
